title: Starlit Entertainment — moderation onramp scratchpad
content:
Context:
Starlit Entertainment (video UGC platform) — want to replace brittle keyword-based filters with a hybrid LLM-based moderation pipeline. They are extremely latency-sensitive for live chat during streams and need deterministic safety for user-facing labels (actionable ban/warn/allow). Customer asks for private deployment option (on their GCP VPC) and FIPS/KMS support for keys controlling safety models.

Call notes (2025-02-11):
- Met with product + safety lead (Jae Kim) and infra lead (Lina Ortiz). They run mixed live chat + comments + clip captions. Typical message lengths 20–120 tokens, but emojis and GIF captions cause odd tokenization spikes.
- Hard requirement: 99.9% of chat moderation decisions must return within 150ms (p95). They will accept async review for non-blocking tags, but bans/warns must be blocking.
- Data retention policy: chat text stored for 48 hours only; audit logs must be exportable to their SIEM.
- They want deterministic rules for appeals: every ban must record model score + fallback rule that triggered.
- Concern: hallucination in explanatory fields; they refuse free-text explanations in ban messages — must be templated.

Technical constraints & gotchas discovered:
- Streaming/real-time path: continuous batching is dangerous if p95 target is 150ms; need micro-batching with max latency cap. For small messages, batching hurts. Suggest route: prefer single-request low-latency route with lightweight quantized model (~4-bit) and fallback to heavier ensemble offline.
- Tokenization emoji problem: some GIF captioning and emoji clusters result in 200+ token sequences even though user-visible length is short. Need a pre-tokenization heuristics layer (collapse emoji clusters, strip zero-width chars) before sending to inference to keep cost/latency predictable.
- Prefix caching not helpful for short chat messages but helpful for threaded comment moderation. Tune caching policy by channel type.
- Model calibration: out-of-the-box safety classifiers show unstable thresholds across domains (slang, regional profanity). Plan a small labeling job (3k examples across genres) to calibrate per-region thresholds and map to discrete actions.
- Explainability: avoid generative rationales. Use model to produce labels + confidence + sparse evidence tokens (indices) that map into their templated messages server-side.
- Private deployment ops: they insist on KMS integration for model keys and audit log forwarding. Need to confirm we support their HSM provider (Thales) or if we rely on cloud KMS.
- Rate limits: bursts during popular streams could spike to 15k req/s for chat moderation. Need autoscale policies and graceful degradation: route to lower-cost coarse classifier or sampling + human review with WebSocket backpressure signals to frontend.

Proposed solution sketch:
1) Two-tier pipeline: fast path (blocking) + slow path (async review)
   - Fast path: redwood-hosted private deployment in their VPC (Redwood Private control plane, worker nodes inside VPC) running a small, low-latency classifier (e.g., distilled safety model quantized). Endpoint tuned to p95 120–140ms with micro-batching disabled; concurrency sharding per channel.
   - Slow path: full ensemble + reranker that runs on dedicated capacity with batched processing to produce richer context + appeals package.
2) Preprocessing layer (edge): normalization, emoji cluster collapse, micro-tokenizer to guarantee token cap (cut and tag overflow as "truncated").
3) Deterministic policy component: maps model label + score band -> action (allow/warn/soft-ban/hard-ban) with templated message IDs (no free text). Logs include model id, score, evidence token indices, and routing decision id for audit.
4) Fallbacks: if Private capacity exhausted, fallback to a compatible hosted-safe model (lower QPS) with explicit degrade flag and sampling to detect drift.

Immediate next steps / action items:
- Asha: draft SOW outline for Private onramp and send draft to Jae by 2025-02-13 (IN-PROGRESS).
- Marco: prototype micro-tokenizer heuristics (emoji collapse) and share benchmark (latency + token count) by 2025-02-17.
- Lina: provide expected peak QPS by channel + existing infra constraints (how many connections per backend) — due 2025-02-14.
- Priya: scope small calibration labeling batch (3k examples across 4 genres) and estimate costs — due 2025-02-20.
- Engineering: quick risk doc on KMS/HSM compatibility needed; confirm Thales integration possibility or recommend cloud KMS fallback — owner TBD.

Risks / open questions:
- Can we guarantee p95 150ms for bans in a private deployment with their expected traffic? Might require reserved capacity (Dedicated) or very conservative concurrency caps.
- Legal: export controls for some clip captions? Flag for security/compliance to review.
- Appeals pipeline: they want every banned message to be persisted for 30 days for appeals, but their retention policy for chat is 48 hours. Need to align with legal on storing ban artifacts.

Notes to self / internal hypotheses:
- Likely move: Dedicated reserved pool for fast path inside their VPC (hybrid billing). That allows predictable SLOs and audit keys but increases their cost — position as SLA-backed option.
- Consider offering a "safety shim" small model we can ship as containerized unit for on-prem if customer wants fully air-gapped. But licensing + model weights may complicate.

Meeting follow-ups planned:
- Technical deep dive with eng-serving-runtime (engineers: Soumya, Arjun) on 2025-02-18 to size worker pools.
- Legal + security sync (Asha + Security) to reconcile retention vs appeals on 2025-02-19.
- Pilot kickoff meeting with Starlit (Jae + Lina + ops) 2025-02-25 — scope: 2-week trial on one channel with low concurrency.

Quick reference links (internal):
- Similar case: music-stream moderation pilot notes: confluence ID ENG-MOD-009 (compare emoji handling notes)
- Internal PR for microtokenizer: github.com/redwood-inference/microtokenizer/pull/7

End of scratchpad.
